verses.text: Praise the LORD! Thank the LORD, because he is good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Who can tell all the mighty things the LORD has done, or praise him as much as he deserves?
Happy are those who do what is fair, who always do what is right.
LORD, remember me when you show kindness to your people. Come and save me,
so I can see your chosen people do well, share in the joy of your nation, and celebrate with the people who belong to you.
We have sinned, just as our ancestors did. We have done wrong. We have done evil.
When our ancestors were in Egypt, they did not understand your miracles. They did not remember your many acts of faithful love. Instead, they rebelled by the sea, the Red Sea.
But he saved them for the honour of his name, to show his mighty power.
He gave a command to the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the deep waters as if they were a desert.
He saved them from those who hated them. He rescued them from the power of the enemy.
The water covered their enemies. Not one of them was left.
Then they believed his promises and sang his praise.
But they quickly forgot what he had done. They did not wait for his advice.
In the wilderness they gave in to their cravings. In the desert they tested God.
So he gave them what they asked for, but he also sent a disease that made them waste away.
In the camp they became jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the LORD's holy priest.
The earth opened up and swallowed Dathan. It buried Abiram and his group.
Fire broke out among their followers. Flames burned up the wicked.
At Mount Horeb they made a calf. They bowed down to a metal idol.
They traded the glory of God for an image of a bull that eats grass.
They forgot God, who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt,
amazing things in the land of Ham, and terrifying things at the Red Sea.
So he said he would destroy them. But Moses, his chosen one, stood in the gap in front of him to turn his anger away, so he would not destroy them.
Then they refused to go into the beautiful land. They did not believe his promise.
They complained in their tents and would not listen to the LORD.
So he lifted his hand and promised that he would make them die in the wilderness,
that he would make their descendants die among the nations and scatter them in other lands.
They joined in worshipping the god Baal at Peor. They ate sacrifices offered to lifeless gods.
They made the LORD angry with what they did, and a terrible disease broke out among them.
But Phinehas stood up and stepped in, and the disease was stopped.
This was counted as right for him, for all generations to come.
At the waters of Meribah they made the LORD angry, and trouble came to Moses because of them.
They rebelled against God's Spirit, and Moses spoke without thinking.
They did not destroy the nations as the LORD had commanded them.
Instead, they mixed with the nations and learned to do what they did.
They worshipped their idols, which became a trap for them.
They even sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
They killed innocent people, their own sons and daughters, and sacrificed them to the idols of Canaan. The land was made unclean by their blood.
They made themselves unclean by what they did. They were unfaithful to God like a woman who sells her body.
So the LORD was furious with his people. He was disgusted with those who belonged to him.
He handed them over to the nations. Those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies crushed them and brought them under their power.
Many times he rescued them, but they kept rebelling against him with their own plans. They sank lower and lower because of their sin.
But he still saw their trouble when he heard their cry.
He remembered his covenant with them. Because of his great and faithful love, he changed his mind.
He made all those who held them captive feel sorry for them.
LORD our God, save us. Gather us from among the nations, so we can thank your holy name and celebrate as we praise you.
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, from forever in the past to forever in the future. Let all the people say, "Amen!" Praise the LORD!
